rubrics.criterion: In the final tree, no single class or owner accumulates multiple unrelated responsibility clusters from this pipeline; the ref-registry/commands concern, defaults/params resolution, the visibility lifecycle with auto-hide scheduling, keyboard observation, layout/animation geometry, swipe gesture handling, and renderer selection are distributed so each concern's implementation is contained in one or more small cohesive owners.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central semantic outcome for this instance: the injected candidate centralizes all of these on the manager class, and redistribution into cohesive owners is the assigned smell focus.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor is not cosmetic centralization: no replacement class, module, or object retains the same concentration of unrelated concerns as the removed coordinator (e.g. all manager members moved into one differently named class, or one new facade into which every existing module still funnels).
rubrics.rationale: A rename or re-wrap that preserves the concentration fails the smell resolution while appearing structurally different, which a pure count-based view would miss.

rubrics.criterion: Imperative command semantics are preserved: the module-level Toast.show/Toast.hide entry points act on the most recently mounted registered toast ref, and refs are (un)registered around mount/unmount and ref changes exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: The imperative API is the library's headline feature; the registry/logic was absorbed into the coordinator, so its re-homed owner must keep the latest-ref semantics the tests rely on.

rubrics.criterion: Show-params and defaults resolution behavior is preserved: base data and base options (including default animation config and any resolution over custom animation configs) are applied with the skip-undefined merge policy, and per-show params can carry custom data/options/props and type.
rubrics.rationale: The resolution logic was absorbed as coordinator statics; a sound re-homing must reproduce the merge semantics exactly or observable toast payloads change.

rubrics.criterion: The visibility lifecycle and auto-hide behavior are preserved: show applies data/options and visibility in the original order with the original log calls; auto-hide is (re)scheduled by the visibility/options effect, honors the no-auto-hide option, and pending timers are cleared on unmount; hide cancels the timer before hiding.
rubrics.rationale: The lifecycle choreography and operation ordering were specified invariants of the injection; extracted owners must not invert state-application, logging, or timer-clearing sequences.

rubrics.criterion: Auto-hide timing remains per-instance and self-sufficient: each mounted toast's timer starts, clears, and reports activity against its own lifecycle state, including the unmount-cleanup path.
rubrics.rationale: The general-purpose timeout hook absorbed scheduling into the coordinator; a valid extraction gives timing its own owner without leaking cross-instance or stale timers.

rubrics.criterion: Keyboard tracking remains correct: listeners are attached only on iOS, detached on cleanup, and consuming components observe keyboard height and visibility exactly as previously.
rubrics.rationale: iOS gating is an environment-dependent invariant; the absorbed observer must be extracted without dropping the platform gate or the state contract.

rubrics.criterion: Slide animation behavior is preserved: translateY output ranges derived from container/toast geometry, position, and animation type; the additive-inverse pacing case; style emission on the same dependency cadence; imperative slide-to and spring-restore behavior; and the animation driver defaults from animation config resolution.
rubrics.rationale: The geometry and driving logic were absorbed as coordinator statics and are pinned by tests; the extracted owner must keep the derivations and driver defaults identical.

rubrics.criterion: Swipe/pan behavior is preserved: start/move responder decision predicates, damping for top-positioned toasts vs others, gesture-delta-driven animated values, the swipe-dismiss threshold and direction logic, and exact callback sequencing including the swipe-end callback firing before the enabled-check in both release and terminate paths.
rubrics.rationale: The gesture dispatch and swipe visuals absorbed by the coordinator are behaviorally subtle (ordering and position-dependence); a sound extraction reproduces both the physics and the callback order.

rubrics.criterion: Renderer selection and rendering behavior are preserved: the per-type renderer lookup keeps caller-supplied config entries overriding the built-in success/error/info renderers and preserves the same failure behavior for unknown or missing types, producing the same rendered output structure and props.
rubrics.rationale: Renderer resolution was absorbed into the coordinator; the re-homed owner must preserve the priority order and failure fallbacks the tests pin.

rubrics.criterion: All rewired consumption sites are updated to their new owners consistently: the primary hook, the toast component pair, the timeout/keyboard/slide-pan/dimension hooks, the animated container, and the utility modules whose exports delegate, so each consumer calls the owner of the concern it needs rather than a leftover all-embracing intermediary.
rubrics.rationale: The injection rewired twelve existing modules into the coordinator; a complete repair rewrites these seams to point at the distributed owners instead of leaving them threaded through one object.

rubrics.criterion: No duplicated live implementations remain: the same responsibility (timer scheduling, geometry/range derivation, damping, merge policy, renderer lookup) is not kept in both the new owner and an old seam as two divergent copies.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that leaves parallel old and new copies passes superficial smoke tests but reintroduces drift risk, which is a concrete failure specific to delegation-heavy refactors.

rubrics.criterion: The stable public import surface still resolves from its original module paths with unchanged names and signatures, including the gesture helpers exported by the animated container module and the bound/merge/animation-config helpers from src/utils.
rubrics.rationale: Consumer compatibility was an explicit constraint; the refactor must not relocate or narrow exports that existing tests and downstream apps import.

rubrics.criterion: No injection-specific dead artifacts remain: the coordinator class file is gone or its members fully re-homed, and no orphaned types, session/binder plumbing, or unused helpers that existed solely to support the coordinator survive in the tree.
rubrics.rationale: The coordinator's session-binding architecture is an artifact of this task's injected candidate; leaving its scaffolding behind half-dead is an incomplete cleanup unique to this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Any retained compatibility wrappers are intentional and uniformly minimal: each retained wrapper still has live consumers and delegates to exactly one real owner, rather than preserving the wrapper-everywhere shape where the util modules and hooks all forward through one class.
rubrics.rationale: Distinguishing deliberate API-stability shims from leftover indirection requires an instance-specific judgment; the injected candidate's tell is wrappers that funnel into a single omniscient class.

rubrics.criterion: Per-mount isolation is not broken: timers, keyboard listeners, responder/session state, and lifecycle data are scoped per mounted toast instance, so two simultaneously mounted toasts never share or clobber each other's pending state.
rubrics.rationale: The coordinator's instance/session split is what kept the pre-existing isolation; naive extraction into module-level singletons is the plausible regression specific to this case.

rubrics.criterion: No stale-closure regressions: extracted code paths that invoke React state appliers, logging, options, panning, or animation callbacks must observe the values from the latest render (or rebind per render), not values captured once at first render or at extraction time.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed coordinator relied on per-render rebinding to stay fresh; extraction is precisely where such callbacks can accidentally freeze, and this failure mode shows up only at runtime with changing props.

rubrics.criterion: Observable operation ordering is not disturbed: log calls fire in their original positions relative to state application and timer work, and interaction callbacks fire in their original sequence (for example the swipe-end callback before the enabled-check).
rubrics.rationale: The ordering guarantees were invariants this candidate was built to preserve; a repair that reshuffles them changes externally visible behavior even while passing basic render tests.
